 Live Updates Updated Thu, Nov 19 2026 2:18 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Dow dives 900 points as Anthropic IPO milestone causes investors to take profits: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Jenny Lee Tanaya Macheel Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, US, Nov. 18, 2026. Brendan McDermid | Reuters Stocks tumbled on Thursday, falling to their lows of the session the very moment the widely anticipated artificial intelligence IPO Anthropic began trading .
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq dropped 1.7% after gaining as much as 2% earlier in the session. The S&P 500 shed 1.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 920 points, or 1.8%. 
 Anthropic , trading at the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, opened shortly before noon at $111.50 per share, a 34% pop. The stock was trading more than 10% off the first trading price and was last up 14%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Nasdaq Composite, 1-day The major averages fell to session lows immediately following the start of trading for the much-hyped IPO, as investors appeared to take profits at the culmination of this moment for the AI trade.
 The artificial intelligence company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range. That had chip stocks and other AI plays jumping in morning trading.
 Chipmakers Nvidia and Micron Technology gave up their gains, along with tech giants Microsoft and Meta Platforms . Advanced Micro Devices lost more than 8% after Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position in the name, pointing to alleged U.S. export control breaches that involve China.
 "This was always going to be a critical test for the tech sector. Anthropic could be the new poster child for AI trade, especially after Nvidia headlines," said Aleks Spencer, Bogart Wealth CIO. "There's a lot here too that needs to be processed and digested, which translates to this period of uncertainty and volatility."
 The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) , or Wall Street's so-called fear gauge, reached a day high of close to 29 — its highest level since March — shortly after Anthropic began trading and investors moved out of tech stocks. The index was last above 27. 
 "The enthusiasm comes in, and it's a great moment to sell the rally and take some profits," Spencer added.
 The market has become more cautious on AI as of late, with investors focusing on whether heavy spending on the buildout will translate into meaningful profits. The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) has fallen 10% this month, and embattled AI bellwether Nvidia has dropped 27% while the company grapples with the resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of CoreWeave, which had seen its bond yields trade above 16% earlier this month, is down 16% in November.
 To be sure, some on Wall Street aren't too alarmed about the rollercoaster ride sparked by Anthropic's debut.
 "Today doesn't matter," said Baird tech strategist Ted Mortonson, who deemed the day's action in Anthropic akin to that of a casino. "It's a blink of an eye of their journey. It's an important event, but how they navigate the next three years that will determine valuation."
 33 Min Ago Interactive Brokers' Sosnick says market moves show 'sell the rally' sentiment after Anthropic's debut
 Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, Nov. 17, 2026 in New York City. Spencer Platt | Getty Images While the major indexes took a leg lower immediately after Anthropic began trading at the Nasdaq, Interactive Brokers' chief strategist Steve Sosnick noted that the premarket rally faded before the artificial intelligence giant began trading. 
 "What we saw before that was the latest round of 'sell the rally' trading that has overtaken the more customary 'buy the dip' in recent days," he said. 
 Sosnick said that the rationale for the drop wasn't clear, though once the S&P 500 was able to break through a key support level in recent days, 7,300, that's when selling accelerated. 
 "The dam seemed to break once the big event was behind us," he added. 
 — Davis Giangiulio 
 1 Hour Ago VIX rises above 27
 The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) topped 27 on Thursday, signaling uncertainty in the U.S. market.
 It was last hovering at 27.94.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon VIX, 1-day The stock market has been volatile as of late as investors have priced in macreconomic and geopolitical uncertainty. On Thursday, Anthropic listed its shares on the Nasdaq, sparking a selloff that rattled many areas of the market. 
 — Liz Napolitano 
 2 Hours Ago S&P 500 deepens dip below 200-day moving average
 The S&P 500 fell further below its 200-day moving average on Thursday as stocks sold off following Anthropic 's initial public offering. 
 The broad-market index was last hovering around 7,273.98. That puts it about 74 points, or roughly 1%, below its 200-day moving average of 7,348.54. 
 "That's a big technical signal," Thomas Martin, a partner and senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments, told CNBC. "It has been above its 200-day moving average for a long time. And, if you're a trend follower, you say, 'okay, well, maybe if it breaks through, you have room to the downside.'"
 The S&P 500's latest decline comes one day after its closed below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 7. 
 Zoom In Icon Arrows pointing outwards FactSet — Liz Napolitano 
 2 Hours Ago Stocks tumble to session lows after Anthropic begins trading
 Stocks rolled over to session lows nearly immediately after Anthropic began trading at the Nasdaq. While the AI giant opened 34% higher, it quickly eased from those levels — as enthusiasm around the company's public market debut withered.
 The Dow tumbled to trade more than 1,000 points lower, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite were down more than 1% each. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Indexes intraday The declines put the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all down more than 3% for the month. Per Bespoke, this would be the first November since 2008 that all major indexes are down that much through Nov. 18. 
 — Fred Imbert 
 3 Hours Ago Anthropic opens at $111.50, up 34.3%, after record-setting $81 billion initial public offering
 Anthropic billboards are displayed in Times Square as shares begin trading after their IPO on November 19, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images Shares in frontier artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic opened at $111.50, up 34.3% from its $83 initial public offering price, after raising a record $81 billion in the largest ever sale of stock by a company entering the public market for the first time.
 At the opening price, Anthropic, led by CEO Dario Amodei, has a fully diluted market capitalization of roughly $2 trillion. San Francisco-based Anthropic trades on the Nasdaq Stock Market under ticker symbol ANT.
 Amodei co-founded Anthropic less than six years ago, in 2021, alongside a handful of other researchers after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. 
 — Scott Schnipper, Ashley Capoot and Leslie Picker 
 4 Hours Ago Anthropic IPO will 'be an important barometer for investors' AI appetite,' Plancorp's Cox says
 CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei and President and co-founder of Anthropic Daniela Amodei, celebrate next to CEO of Nasdaq Adena Friedman as Anthropic, PBC (ANT) holds their initial public offering (IPO) at the NASDAQ MarketSite in New York City, US, November 19, 2026. Brendan Mcdermid | Reuters Anthropic's debut on Thursday will serve as a key measure of just how much investors remain bullish on the artificial intelligence trade.
 "It'll be an important barometer for investors' AI appetite," said Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp. "AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations."
 "The challenge in that thesis is that hot IPOs rarely perform well right out of the gate, especially these days, when every company seems to be vying for a limited pool of capital to fund their AI strategy," she said. "While I wouldn't be surprised to see the stock market take cues from Anthropic's performance, I'd caution investors about trying to read the tea leaves from one event too much."
 — Tanaya Macheel 
 4 Hours Ago Anthropic proxies up just ahead of IPO 
 Enthusiasm around the Anthropic IPO is lifting the broader tech trade, especially those stocks that are direct proxies for the AI company. Here are the latest moves:
 Amazon up less than 1% 
 Alphabet up almost 3% 
 Broadcom up more than 1% 
 — Sarah Min 
 5 Hours Ago JPMorgan downgrades Alphabet bonds
 JPMorgan downgraded Alphabet corporate bonds to neutral from overweight, noting that "tighter valuations leave less room for outperformance relative to Amazon."
 "Our base case assumes strong growth and eventual improvement in cash conversion, but [free cash flow] remains negative through 2028, requiring further financing while substantial liquidity and earnings keep leverage low," wrote credit analyst Erica Spear. "Alphabet's quarter exposed a widening divergence between accelerating Cloud demand and slowing Search growth, with weaker monetization of AI queries adding to uncertainty around the core earnings engine."
 — Fred Imbert 
 5 Hours Ago Stocks open higher
 The three major averages began Thursday's session in positive territory.
 The Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.5% just after 9:30 a.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 230 points, or 0.4%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 5 Hours Ago Gold hits lowest level since September 2025, pacing for another weekly loss
 Gold dore bars stacked at the Perth Mint Refinery, operated by Gold Corp., in Perth, Australia, on Thursday, Feb. 5, 2026. Matt Jelonek | Bloomberg | Getty Images U.S. gold futures for December delivery hit a low of $3,694.5 on Thursday, before recovering slightly to back above $3,700. 
 The low represented a level that the metal hasn't traded at since September 2025. 
 Gold is currently down 4.4% on the week, and tracking for its second straight weekly loss and the fifth negative one in six. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) was down 1% in premarket trading Thursday. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Gold 5-day. — Gina Francolla and Davis Giangiulio 
 6 Hours Ago Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index falls more than expected
 Factory activity in the Philadelphia area expanded at a slower pace in November while employment showed strength and prices received rose at the fastest pace in more than four years, the regional Federal Reserve reported Thursday.
 The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index moved lower to 6.3, off more than 14 points from October for the lowest reading since May. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had been looking for a reading of 18 for a gauge that measures the difference between companies reporting growth and contraction.
 Within the survey, the employment index rose 3 points to 11.6, its first increase in three months, while the prices paid measure jumped 15 points to 58.2, its highest going back to April. Similarly, the prices received index surged 7 points to 47, the highest level since June 2022.
 — Jeff Cox 
 6 Hours Ago Jobless claims top forecast
 Job seekers check-in to a job fair at a Schneider Electric manufacturing facility in Hopkins, South Carolina, US, on Wednesday, Jan. 18, 2023. Micah Green | Bloomberg | Getty Images Initial jobless claims edged higher last week but were still within the recent range showing that the pace of layoffs remains low.
 The Labor Department reported Thursday that first-time filings for unemployment benefits for the week ending Nov. 14 totaled a seasonally adjusted 203,000, up just 1,000 from the prior period but higher than the Dow Jones consensus estimate for 197,000.
 Continuing claims, which run a week behind, rose 70,000 to 1.76 million.
 — Jeff Cox 
 6 Hours Ago Anthropic proxies jump in the premarket
 Anthropic proxies jumped ahead of the AI company's IPO. Here are the premarket moves:
 Amazon and Alphabet climbed 2.4% and 4.1%, respectively. The two companies each have sizable investments in Anthropic. In April, Amazon agreed to invest up to $25 billion in the company. That same month, Google said it plans to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic . 
 Broadcom rose 2.9%. Last month, the chipmaker announced a special purpose vehicle to finance $63 billion in chips and networking products to be leased to Anthropic. 
 — Sarah Min 
 7 Hours Ago Texas resuming data center permits is adding momentum to equity futures, Boockvar says
 The latest decision by environmental regulators in Texas to resume reviewing data center permits has given a boost to equity futures in addition to the Anthropic IPO, said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners.
 "Not just the very successful IPO of Anthopic but the news too that the Texas Department of Environmental Quality 'has gathered information for the community impact review for pending data center projects. The agency has resumed its normal permit review process and will evaluate applications under all applicable state and federal laws and regulations' has the futures rallying sharply this morning," he wrote.
 Futures tied to the Nasdaq-100 gained more than 2% early Thursday, led by chipmakers as well as key "Magnificent Seven" names. S&P 500 futures rose more than 1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were up around 300 points, or 0.6%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 7 Hours Ago Walmart's muted guidance hike could indicate a cautious holiday season quarter
 A Walmart sign hangs on a cart outside the store on August 20, 2026, in Miami, Florida. Joe Raedle | Getty Images A somewhat mundane double beat from Walmart – with third quarter EPS only beating by a penny, while revenues topped estimates by a little more than $1.5 billion.
 But Walmart U.S. same-store sales failed to beat Wall Street expectations for the second straight quarter. It came just dead in line at up 2.9% for the third quarter, while it cleanly missed estimates last quarter.
 The retail giant raised its full year guidance. But just like many of the other major retail reports this week, it's a pretty tepid hike, particularly on the earnings front. The new adjusted EPS range of $2.84-$2.89 is up from a prior forecast of $2.80-2.87. But more importantly, that new forecast implies Q4 adj. EPS of 72- 77 cents, clearly below 79 cents est.
 — Robert Hum 
 8 Hours Ago Oil prices tick higher after reports of strikes on Gulf nations
 Front-month Brent crude oil futures were 0.5% higher at $92.43 a barrel on Thursday morning, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were 0.6% higher at $83.74. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Crude oil futures Oil prices have cooled in recent weeks amid hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the U.S.-Iran war. 
 But concerns about an escalation in the conflict resurged on Thursday, following reports of a series of strikes across the Gulf. 
 The PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district — belonging to Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund — was hit by a missile, according to Reuters sources. CNBC has contacted Saudi authorities for comment. 
 Saudi Arabia has been targeted by a series of strikes carried out by the Houthis, a militant group backed by Tehran, in recent weeks, with offices of oil giant Saudi Aramco also coming under attack in recent weeks. 
 Reuters also reported Wednesday that Iran had targeted a U.S. air base in Kuwait and launched several attacks on Bahrain. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 9 Hours Ago Anthropic proxies rise in pre-market
 Shares of companies broadly seen as proxies for Anthropic moved higher in pre-market trading. 
 Amazon and Alphabet , which have made independent investments in the Claude chatbot developer, gained 2% and 3.4%, respectively. 
 Shares of chipmaker Broadcom , a major partner of Anthropic, were last seen trading 2.8% ahead of Thursday's opening bell. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 10 Hours Ago Take-Two shares pull back after surging on GTA 6 release
 Commuters walk past advertising billboards for the game "Grand Theft Auto VI" in a hallway at Kings Cross underground station, in central London on November 11, 2026. Henry Nicholls | Afp | Getty Images Shares of Take-Two Interactive Software — the parent company of Rockstar Games, which makes the "Grand Theft Auto" video game franchise — were down by around 0.3% in pre-market trading on Thursday. 
 The stock surged more than 6% in Wednesday's regular trading session, after the release of the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI. 
 Loading chart...
 Take-Two's Nasdaq-listed shares are down around 18.5% from their July high, and 15.4% year-to-date, with delays to the sixth instalment in the GTA franchise and broad tech volatility weighing on the stock. 
 A Sensor Tower tracker estimated more than 17 million units of the game had been sold as of early Wednesday, exceeding pre-order volumes of all the biggest video game releases in recent history.
 The game became available in the U.S. on Thursday, unlocking across the country on a midnight rollout. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 10 Hours Ago Bank of France chief says market’s budget concerns an ‘overreaction’
 watch now VIDEO 3:08 03:08 Bank of France Gov: Deficit and debt are too high and can’t be ignored Squawk Box Europe The head of France's central bank told CNBC he is confident there will be a budget put in place for next year, despite political divisions creating an impasse in talks among lawmakers.  
 A draft budget proposed by Prime Minister Emmanuel Moulin's government, which aimed to drastically cut spending, was unanimously rejected by lawmakers in France's National Assembly last month. 
 French government bonds, known as OATs, have come under intense pressure this year, with borrowing costs surging to multi-decade highs as the Iran war pulled global bond yields higher and investors became increasingly concerned about France's fiscal picture. The spread over German debt has touched on levels not seen since the euro zone debt crisis.
 Speaking to CNBC's Charlotte Reed in Paris, Banque de France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said he thought there had been an "overreaction" within financial markets. 
 "Spreads are high, very high, and too high — they are too high compared with the situation of the French economy, but also its fiscal situation, which is not good, which needs to be dealt with, but which has not changed materially from June to September," he explained. "But I think it's important for the government to give signs that they are serious about reducing the deficit."
 Moulin said the government had put forward a budget aimed at decreasing the French budget deficit from 5.4% of GDP to 5% of GDP.
 "I am quite confident that the budget will be implemented," he said. "I am not sure it will be voted [through] by Parliament because there is no majority and it's quite polarized, but there are other ways to have the budget adopted."
 Since 2024′s snap election delivered a hung parliament, successive governments have used Article 49.3 of the constitution to force budgets through without a vote.
 But threats of motions of no confidence have previously forced concessions. If a government is ousted, lawmakers must go back to the drawing board with the budget.
 Another option is to pass the budget by ordinance, which has never been done in the French Fifth Republic, created in 1958. If a government is ousted after using this power, the budget it forces through remains in place.
 Lecornu secured the 2026 budget via Article 49.3, after replacing ousted Prime Minister François Bayrou. 
 "This is, I think, the two routes that the governments is looking at," Moulin told CNBC. 
 —  Chloe Taylor 
 11 Hours Ago European shares open higher as Anthropic hype drives tech stocks rebound
 Europe-listed shares were broadly higher Thursday morning, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 index adding 0.3% in early trading.
 The Stoxx 600 Technology index jumped 1.4% shortly after the opening bell, rebounding from five consecutive sessions of losses. 
 It comes after Wall Street's tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose on Wednesday, despite a sell-off of Nvidia stock. European chip stocks rallied Thursday morning, with Be Semiconductor , ASML , ASMI and Infineon all adding around 3%. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 11 Hours Ago Japan leads gains in Asia as markets close mixed
 Asia-Pacific markets ended mixed Thursday, with South Korean stocks reversing earlier losses to close higher.
 Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.71% to close at 59,444.21, while the Topix fell 1.53% to 3,822.47.
 South Korea's Kospi rebounded from earlier losses to close 1.39% higher at 5,137.89, while the small-cap Kosdaq gained 3.32% to 684.81.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 1% to close at 8,730.4.
 Mainland China's CSI 300 ended flat at 3,984.84, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 2.04% as of its last hour of trade
 — Jenny Lee  
 12 Hours Ago Resolution to Strait of Hormuz crisis could ‘usher in buyers’ market’ for oil: IEA
 The International Energy Agency said Thursday that a resolution to this year's energy crisis "could usher in a buyers' market for oil and natural gas, with significant downward pressures on prices."
 "The prospects and timing of any resolution are highly uncertain but, if constraints on flows through the Strait of Hormuz are decisively eased, market balances could switch," the industry body said in its flagship World Energy Outlook report. 
 Oil has cooled off from its wartime highs of well above $100 a barrel, but still trades at elevated prices.
 The IEA also noted in its report that confidence in the Strait of Hormuz "has been shattered."
 "Additional bypass projects are moving ahead, but it will not be easy or quick to manage without oil shipments through this strategic waterway," it said. 
 New pipeline projects are under construction or consideration to enhance Gulf producers' ability to reach international markets without transiting the strait, the IEA said. 
 "Building them would require an estimated USD 40 billion, adding around USD 2 to the cost of a barrel of oil exported from the Middle East," it said in the report. "If all these projects are completed, non-Gulf producers step up output, and importers bring down demand as in the ARC, then our Low Hormuz Case reduces the need for transit through the Strait to 2 mb/d by 2035."
 — Chloe Taylor 
 14 Hours Ago Goldman Sachs brings forward New Zealand rate hike forecast to December
 Goldman Sachs now expects New Zealand's central bank to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December, bringing forward its previous forecast for a February hike following increasingly hawkish comments from Reserve Bank of New Zealand officials, according to its note on Thursday. 
 The investment bank expects the official cash rate to reach 3% in December, followed by another 25 basis point hike in March. However, Goldman said the December decision could be more finely balanced than market pricing suggests, with the outlook dependent on economic developments ahead of the central bank's Dec. 9 meeting.
 — Jenny Lee 
 15 Hours Ago Tencent shares fall over 6% as AI spending surges, profit declines 
 Shares of Chinese tech giant Tencent fell 6.71% on Thursday after the company reported a decline in third-quarter profit amid surging investments in artificial intelligence.
 Tencent's revenue rose 8% year on year to 207.3 billion yuan ($31.1 billion), while operating profit fell 6% to 68.1 billion yuan. Capital expenditure payments surged 225% to 65.1 billion yuan, while free cash flow turned negative at 69.1 billion yuan as the company ramped up spending on AI computing resources.
 — Jenny Lee  
 16 Hours Ago ‘Parasite’ backer, other Korean stocks rally on China trade deal
 South Korean entertainment, gaming and travel stocks surged Thursday after Seoul and Beijing announced a breakthrough in trade negotiations, raising hopes of greater access to China's vast consumer market following nearly a decade of restrictions on Korean cultural content.
 Drama producer Studio Dragon soared 29.96%, while CJ ENM, which backed the Oscar-winning film "Parasite," jumped 26%. Travel agency Hana Tour rose 18% and film distributor Showbox gained 9%, while gaming stocks Krafton and Shift Up advanced 2.69% and 6.57%, respectively.
 The two countries largely concluded negotiations to expand their free trade agreement covering services and investment after more than eight years of talks, South Korea's trade ministry said Wednesday. The agreement has yet to be formally signed or take effect.
 — Jenny Lee  
 18 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi drops after markets open late due to college entrance exam
 South Korea's Kospi fell 1.16%, with the small-cap Kosdaq also declining over 1% Thursday, as markets opened an hour later than usual to accommodate the country's annual college entrance exam . 
 Index heavyweights Samsung and SK Hynix were down 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively.
 Trading in South Korea will close an hour later than usual.
 Taiwan's benchmark Taiex declined 0.42%. 
 — Jenny Lee  
 19 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei 225 opens higher, Australian benchmark extends declines
 Asia-Pacific markets opened mixed on Thursday, after Nvidia shares slid on Wall Street overnight.
 Japan's Nikkei 225 inched 0.54% higher, while the Topix fell 0.32%. South Korea's markets will open an hour late due to a college entrance exam 
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 1.12%.
 — Jenny Lee 
 20 Hours Ago Asia markets set for subdued open after Wall Street closes mixed 
 Asia-Pacific markets appeared set for a subdued open Thursday, following a mixed session on Wall Street overnight that saw Nvidia shares slide.
 Futures for Japan's Nikkei 225 in Chicago were at 59,230, compared with the index's previous close of 59,024.28.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 23,100 compared with the index's last close of 23,294.75.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 1.19% in early trade. 
 — Jenny Lee 
 20 Hours Ago Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, source tells CNBC
 Gabby Jones | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, above the expected range, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.
 The AI company, along with its seven co-founders, reportedly upsized the offering, sellling 979.6 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
 For more, read the full story here .
 — Tanaya Macheel, Ashley Capoot and Leslie Picker 
 20 Hours Ago Stock futures open flat
 U.S. equity futures were near the flat line on Wednesday night.
 Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 35 points, or 0.07%. S&P 500 futures added 0.1%, as did Nasdaq 100 futures .
 — Tanaya Macheel
